      "Field-scale spatial heterogeneity and macropore/preferential flow",

    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 6,
  "n_justification": "Six columns span the dominant USDA texture classes found in the Upper Iowa River agricultural landscape (from coarse sandy soils near the river terraces to fine silty clay loams on uplands). Holding location, climate forcing, and PFT constant while stepping through textures cleanly isolates the textural control on sub-surface drainage.",
  "columns": [

  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "2000",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2014",

      "QDRAI",

  "assumptions": [

feasibility.verdict: Feasible with single-column ELM (optionally coupled to PFLOTRAN) by holding climate/vegetation fixed and varying only soil texture across columns to isolate the textural control on sub-surface drainage.
answerable: Sensitivity of sub-surface (gravity) drainage flux to USDA soil texture class
Differences in soil moisture profiles, water table depth, and saturated hydraulic conductivity effects across textures
Partitioning of precipitation into runoff vs. drainage vs. ET as a function of texture
Relative strength (rank/magnitude) of texture control versus a fixed forcing baseline
not_answerable: Effects of artificial tile drainage networks (not represented in default ELM physics)
Lateral groundwater flow / hillslope routing between columns (single-column assumption)
Field-scale spatial heterogeneity and macropore/preferential flow
Actual observed streamflow at the basin outlet (requires routing + calibration)

parsed.n_justification: Six columns span the dominant USDA texture classes found in the Upper Iowa River agricultural landscape (from coarse sandy soils near the river terraces to fine silty clay loams on uplands). Holding location, climate forcing, and PFT constant while stepping through textures cleanly isolates the textural control on sub-surface drainage.
assumptions: All columns share identical atmospheric forcing, PFT (managed C3/rainfed crop or grass), and topography so that only soil texture differs.
A multi-year accelerated + final spinup precedes the 15-year analysis period to equilibrate soil moisture and water table.
Soil texture is set uniformly through the soil column per case; organic layer and bedrock depth held at default.
Default ELM baseflow/drainage parameterization (SIMTOP-style) is used; PFLOTRAN coupling can be enabled for richer variably-saturated subsurface flow but is not required to rank textural sensitivity.
Artificial subsurface tile drainage is not represented; QDRAI represents natural gravity drainage.
Column coordinates are representative of the mid-basin near Decorah, Iowa (~43.3N, 91.8W).
